findings: Separating the known grading stage alone did not improve the six-view student; its validation errors increased.
Adding twelve translated camera views improved both validation errors at 1500 and 4500 steps. The validation images remained outside training.
At 4500 steps, width32 improved mean training error but worsened both validation errors relative to width16. Width alone does not resolve generalization in this dataset.
The fused grading implementation reduced complete student graph cost without changing the tested outputs; this is not native NVIDIA runtime acceleration.
limitations: Only one scene and first-reset frames; no independent cross-scene, motion, disocclusion, skin or UI acceptance.
These two camera validation views have guided repeated research choices and are not an independent final test set.
RGB metrics and FFT bands are diagnostics, not proof of perceptual or temporal equivalence.
Torch graph times exclude D3D12 integration; no student was installed in a game or the native application benchmark.
Grade parameters observed in the same runtime/control configuration are reused on other camera views by inference.
The 1500-step six-view grading run predates the optional all-training-view evaluation; its original-frame error is not an average across all training views.
Source and numerical evidence only; derivative weights and captured images remain private.

paper_followup.title: Deep Bilateral Learning for Real-Time Image Enhancement
paper_followup.idea: Separate compact content-dependent color transforms from full-resolution detail processing.
paper_followup.limit: Pointwise affine transformation assumptions cannot represent all newly created detail; our current student is not an HDRNet implementation.
